newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Leading Russian shares tick up, finding support.
newsitem.headline: Leading Russian shares tick up, finding support.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed slightly up on Wednesday on light trading and speculative interest from investors, traders said.
Some traders said the market had fallen to support levels but investors were still skittish.
The Russian Trading Systems 23-share index nudged up 0.13 percent to close at 303.71 after 303.33 on Tuesday on $19.3 million total market turnover.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's short-term interest rate hike had little effect on the market, which had already priced in the rise, dealers said.
Shares of natural monopolies had the highest dollar value turnovers and closed up. Top government officials offered details of monopoly reform plans early in the afternoon.

Power utility Unified Energy System UES EESR.RTS, rose to $0.1943 from $0.1900 at midday and $0.1930 on Tuesday. Gazprom GAZP.RTS natural gas monopoly ended at $0.678, up from about $0.649 late on Tuesday.
"There's still a lot of nervousness in the market. The European markets are going up and ours will consolidate," said Pavel Gronbjerg, director of corporate securities at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
He said the short Easter week and a day of strikes and protest planned for Thursday would slow trade.
Regent European Securities trader Aleksei Rozhkov said trade had picked up in the afternoon when falling shares found support from operators and short-term investors.
"It's true that people are selling. But UES only gets more attractive the more prices fall," said a trader at a Western bank.
Regional electric company Mosenergo rallied to $1.275 from $1.264, despite what dealers said were mixed reactions to company's financial figures released today.
"One can only assume that some people are covering their short-term positions and, of course, the mood of the market does not really lend itself to a fall," the trader at the Western bank said.
